To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of the coherent growth of GaP/Si substrates for photon and photovoltaic applications.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of coherent growth of III-V/GaP based quantum dots and quantum wells onto Si substrates.

we have developed and optimised GaP/Si heterostructures for photonics and PV applications, and that GaAsP(N) quantum well structures are suitable for the 1310 nm telecom and the datacom optical segments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth and the characterisation of III-V/GaP and (In,Ga,As)As/GaAsN nanostructures grown on GaP and GaP/Silicon pseudo substrate.
the development of III-N-V/GaP nanostructures for photonics and PV applications.
the structural and optical characterization of selected MBE-grown III-Nitride nanostructures on GaP substrated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GaP substrate is a highly promising material for the coherent integration of photonic and PV devices on silicon.
the GaP/Silicon technology is a promising route for the coherent integration of photonically enhanced photovoltaic cells onto silicon substrates.
the GaP substrate and GaP/SI pseudo substrate are suitable for coherent growth of III-V nanostructures for photonics and PV applications, provided the interface is properly optimised.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility to grow GaP based nanostructured layers on silicon, which are suitable for photonics and PV applications.

GaP based nano-structures grown on silicon are a promising route for coherent integration and hybridisation of photonic and high efficiency photovolatic devices onto silicon substrate, and that GaAsPN/GaN heterostructures are a promising route to develop PV devices with higher efficiency.

we have demonstrated the possibility of integrating GaP based nano-structures onto GaP and GaP/Silicon substrates, with the aim of coherent integration of photoncis and photovoltaics onto Silicon substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

GaP based nanostructure grown on silicon substrated is a viable route for coherent integration and that the GaP substrate is an excellent choice for light emission applications, in the 0.8 to 1.3 µm range.
GaP based nano- and microstructures grown on silicon is a promising route for coherent integration and for the development of high performance devices for both photonics and PV applications.
GaP based nanostructure grown on silicon substrats is a highly rewarding route for coherent integration on silicon substrates of photonic and PV devices.
